cohort: The study participants were primiparous adolescents aged 10 to 19 years.
finding: Episiotomy was associated with lower mean values for pelvic floor strength, endurance, and contractions, and significantly increased the odds of urinary incontinence, urinary incontinence-related quality of life changes, fecal incontinence, and constipation in primiparous adolescents.
mod_finding: Episiotomy negatively influenced pelvic floor function and increased the odds of urinary incontinence, fecal incontinence, and constipation in primiparous adolescents.
